So let's just say that you have a boat and want to navigate the Pacific. That's very hard to do and usually requires a computer because of the vast amount of information needed for navigation.

What's amazing about Polynesian people is their ability to settle the entire Pacific, wherever there's an island. This demonstrates our desire to explore the world. How they navigated the Pacific was by building small boats that allowed them to get to islands quickly. They read stars in their heads and memorized oceanic currents to determine their position.

So much information needed constant attention: wind, oceanic currents, and stars. Without computers, they had maps of stars and oceanic currents but did all calculations mentally. While at sea, the navigator couldn't sleep; falling asleep meant getting lost and dying.

The myth that we evolved from apes is about more than just our bodies; our minds came from somewhere else, shaping our evolution. School teaches us this to justify power hierarchies where those in charge are seen as stronger and better fit.

The pyramids were built 2400 BCE, not by aliens or lost civilizations but by people with an imaginative mind capable of complex construction. The pyramids aren't tombs; they're temples, and their construction involved intricate debates and techniques.
